title: Identification and quantification of volatile organic compounds in vegetation leaves using HS-SPME and GC-MS
author: Nicolas Younes
materials: Standards, from lowest to highest concentration.

steps.title: Open headspace vial
steps.instruction: Remove the cap of a 20 mL headspace vial.

steps.title: Collect leaf material
steps.instruction: Using a hole punch, collect five punches of equal size from the leaf, preferably on either side of the main vein and along the longest axis. If the leaf is too small for punches, weigh the whole mature leaf, measure its area, and place it at the bottom of the vial to avoid direct contact with the SPME fibre. For spiny species such as Ulex europaeus, cut the distal third of a branchlet, measure the cut area, place the whole piece into the vial and push it to the bottom.

substeps.instruction: If leaf too small, weigh whole leaf, measure area, push to bottom.
If spiny species, cut distal third, measure area, place whole piece, push to bottom.

steps.title: Seal and label vial
steps.instruction: Using latex gloves, reseal the 20 mL headspace vial, label the side with adhesive labels and markers, store the sealed vial in a cool, sun‑sheltered place (if possible at –20 °C), and avoid touching the cap septum with gloves.

steps.title: Collect field control
steps.instruction: Open a new 20 mL headspace vial, expose it to ambient air by moving around the sampling area, reseal with latex gloves, label as “field control sample” for the site, store in a cool, sun‑sheltered place (if possible at –20 °C), and avoid touching the septum.

steps.title: Store collected samples
steps.instruction: Place all sealed vials (leaf samples and field controls) in a –20 °C freezer until analysis. Repeat the collection steps until all required samples are obtained.

steps.title: Prepare standard solutions
steps.instruction: Using methanol as diluent, prepare individual dilutions of β‑pinene, eucalyptol, Cannabis Terpene Mix A, and Cannabis Terpene Mix B at concentrations of 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, and 1000 µg mL⁻¹ in separate 20 mL headspace vials.

steps.title: Aliquot standard volumes
steps.instruction: For each concentration of each standard, pipette 10 µL into a new 20 mL labelled headspace vial.

steps.title: Store standards
steps.instruction: Keep all standard aliquots and the original dilution vials at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Equilibrate samples
steps.instruction: Remove vials from the –20 °C freezer and allow them to reach room temperature (approximately 10 minutes). Process only the samples selected for that day.

steps.title: Program GC‑MS method
steps.instruction: Set instrument operating conditions and method parameters as listed in Table 1 (SPME GC‑MS method parameters). Seal at least four empty 20 mL headspace vials to serve as blank quality‑control samples.

steps.title: Load sampling rack
steps.instruction: Place standards, field‑control vials, blanks, and leaf sample vials randomly onto the sampling rack to minimise systematic bias.

steps.title: Run SPME‑GC‑MS sequence
steps.instruction: For each vial perform: sample equilibration 20 min, fibre adsorption 20 min, GC‑MS run 26 min, fibre post‑bake 10 min, oven cool‑down 10 min (total cycle ≈86 min per sample).

steps.title: Process data with MassHunter
steps.instruction: Use MassHunter Quantitative Analysis version 10.0 to create a new quantitative method (new method with acquired scan data). Set the base‑peak as the quant ion, add four qualifier ions, define a retention‑time window of –0.1 min to +0.2 min, select the “find by deconvolution” method, import calibration curves for each compound, and run the method on all samples, standards, and blanks. Export the results.

substeps.instruction: Create new method with acquired scan data.
Set retention‑time window (‑0.1 min left, +0.2 min right).
Import calibration curves and link to compounds.
Run method on all files and export outputs.

steps.title: Quantify terpenes
steps.instruction: Select a standard concentration (e.g., 500 µg µL⁻¹) for all four standards to detect compounds in the GC‑MS data file, then manually review the output for errors and for peaks without known concentrations. Use the calibration curves to identify and quantify each terpene in eucalyptus leaf samples; each sample, standard, and control vial should yield a chromatogram with identifiable retention times.
